subject: Starter→Enterprise commitment blueprint and onboarding steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Starter→Enterprise commitment blueprint and onboarding steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really appreciated the candid signal on peak usage patterns and the team’s timeline for production later this year. Attached is a concise blueprint that maps Starter / Growth / Enterprise commit tiers to the entitlements and onboarding milestones we discussed. High level: 

- Starter (0.5M tokens/month avg): entry pricing, 30-day onboarding, shared support, basic SLAs.
- Growth (2M tokens/month avg): tiered unit discounts (list below), 30–60 day onboarding with 1:1 onboarding lead, retention of prefix cache config.
- Enterprise (8M+ tokens/month avg): deepest per-token discounts, dedicated capacity option, custom SLOs, SOC-2 evidence package included.

Discount bands in the attached are illustrative; two levers we can push independently are (A) unit price by commit, and (B) entitlements (dedicated capacity / improved SLO / longer data retention). For quick reference inside the PDF I included a sample ramp schedule and a short onboarding checklist with owner names.

Next steps I propose:
1) You and procurement flag which tier best aligns with your FY27 forecast (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) by EOD Thu.
2) We’ll convert the chosen tier to a draft SOW (Ben) and a billing schedule.
3) If Enterprise, we’ll schedule a security handoff for SOC-2 artifacts and a 1-week dedicated onboarding kickoff.

Attachment: AnnualCommit_Blueprint_v1.pdf (PDF)

If you want, I can prepare a blended option (Growth for year 1 with Enterprise breakpoints at 6 months) — works well when adoption is uneven across product teams.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

---

From: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@brighthealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Patel <evan.patel@brighthealth.com>, procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Starter→Enterprise commitment blueprint and onboarding steps

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A couple quick points from our side: 

- We like the Growth tier shape but need clarification on the overage treatment. Does the per-token overage bill at the next slab or at list? We need predictable overage calculations for our finance team.
- On entitlements: the Enterprise dedicated capacity plus 99.95% regional SLO is attractive, but we’d want assurance on failover behavior if our region has an outage.
- Can you also confirm whether prefix/KV cache is preserved across model minor-version rollouts? That affects latency for chat-heavy workflows.

If you can update the blueprint with explicit overage math and a short failover note, we’ll route to procurement and try to indicate a preferred tier by Friday.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations, BrightHealth
ajohnson@brighthealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Starter→Enterprise commitment blueprint and onboarding steps

Jasmine / Ben — looping in quick internal notes before we send a formal update to Alex: 

1) Overage math: propose to charge overage at the next breakpoint unit price (i.e., if they commit Growth and exceed Growth slab, overage billed at Growth+10% unit price up to Enterprise threshold) — keeps predictability and encourages moving to the next tier. We should document exact formula and an example.
2) Failover SLOs: we can guarantee regional SLOs and provide automatic routing to secondary region as part of Enterprise, but cross-region transient latency/latency spikes should be excluded from financial credit. We will provide detailed runbook in the SOW.
3) Cache persistence: prefix/KV cache persists across minor model versions for hosted API — we keep the same KV key format for minor releases; major model architecture changes may invalidate caches. Add that text.

I drafted a short paragraph for the updated blueprint and flagged the PDF to include a worked example of overage math. Ben — can you draft the SOW + billing schedule (net30 by default) and include the ramp payment options (monthly smoothing vs upfront credits)? If procurement pushes for net45, we can offer net45 for Growth+ only with a 2% admin fee.

Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: BrightHealth - draft SOW and billing options

Alex — attaching a short SOW and two billing schedules for BrightHealth. I tried to keep things simple:

- Option A (Growth): 2M token/mo effective commit, billed monthly, net30. Per-token price = $0.0009. Overage billed at Growth+10% per token, capped at Enterprise unit price.
- Option B (Enterprise blended): 8M token/mo effective commit with 6-month ramp (2M / 3M / 8M), 60% upfront credit with monthly reconciliation. Per-token price = $0.0006 after credit amortization; dedicated capacity option available for an added surcharge.

SLA/failover language: Enterprise tier includes automatic cross-region routing as failover; operational credits apply for sustained downtime beyond the SLO window. Transient latency fluctuations are excluded. Cache persistence paragraph included under Operations.

Attachments: BrightHealth_SOW_draft.docx (DOCX), BrightHealth_Billing_Options.xlsx (XLSX)

Action items:
- If Option A works, we can sign and start onboarding in 30 days.
- If Option B, procurement needs the 60% PO and we schedule the security evidence handoff.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement to walk through the financial schedule.

Best,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <ajohnson@brighthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Patel <evan.patel@brighthealth.com>, procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 18:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth - draft SOW and billing options

Thanks Ben — the SOW + billing options are clear and much appreciated. Procurement prefers Option A (Growth) with the overage approach you described; they asked that we keep the option to convert to Enterprise at 30 days notice.

Two small asks before we sign: 
1) Add a one-sentence clause that the KV/prefix cache behavior is guaranteed for minor model updates.
2) Include our standard PO language for net30 in the SOW appendix (I attached it to procurement).

If you can send an updated SOW with those two additions by Monday AM, procurement will prepare the PO and we’ll aim to start onboarding June 22.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

—Alex
